statement: The story takes place in a small town called Maycomb.
Atticus Finch is a doctor.
explanation: Atticus is a lawyer.

statement: Scout tells the story.
Scout's mother looks after the family at home.
explanation: Scout's mother died when Scout was two. Calpurnia helps to look after the children.

statement: Jem is Scout's older brother.
The story takes place in a big city in the north of the USA.
explanation: Maycomb is a small town in Alabama, in the south of the USA.

statement: Calpurnia cooks for the Finch family.
Boo Radley often walks around the town in the daytime.
explanation: Nobody in town has seen Boo outside his house for years.

statement: Dill stays with his aunt in Maycomb in the summer.
Aunt Alexandra is Atticus's mother.
explanation: Aunt Alexandra is Atticus's sister.

statement: Scout enjoys her first day at school.
explanation: Her first day goes badly. Her teacher is cross with her more than once.

statement: Scout can read before she starts school.
The children find presents in a hole in a tree.
Miss Maudie hates working in her garden.
explanation: Miss Maudie loves her garden and spends most of her time in it.

statement: Atticus shoots a mad dog with one shot.
Atticus is a young man who likes to play football.
explanation: Atticus is nearly fifty. He says he is too old to play football.

statement: Bob Ewell is Mayella's father.
Atticus wins Tom Robinson's case.
explanation: The jury finds Tom guilty.

statement: Boo Radley attacks Jem and Scout on Halloween.
explanation: Bob Ewell attacks them. Boo Radley saves them.

statement: At the end of the story, Scout stands on the Radley porch.
Dill dares Jem to run up and touch the Radley house.
Miss Caroline is pleased that Scout can already read.
explanation: She tells Scout that her father must stop teaching her.

statement: Walter Cunningham comes to school without any lunch.
Dill tells the adults the truth about how Jem lost his trousers.
explanation: Dill makes up a story about a game of strip poker.

statement: Jem loses his trousers on the Radley fence.
When Jem goes back for his trousers, someone has mended them.
Jem is happy when Nathan Radley fills the hole in the tree with cement.
explanation: Jem is very upset. Scout can see that he has been crying.

statement: During the fire, someone puts a blanket around Scout without her noticing.
Scout fights her cousin Francis at Christmas.
Atticus has often told his children that he is a good shot.
explanation: He has never mentioned it. The children only find out when he shoots the mad dog.

statement: Mrs Dubose is always polite to Jem and Scout.
explanation: She is rude to them and says cruel things about Atticus.

statement: Calpurnia takes Jem and Scout to her church.
Calpurnia speaks in the same way at church as she does at the Finches' house.
explanation: She speaks differently with the people at her church.

statement: Dill runs away from home and hides under Scout's bed.
Jem and Scout go to the trial because Atticus tells them to.
explanation: They go without asking him.

statement: At the trial, the children sit downstairs with the white people.
explanation: They sit in the balcony with Reverend Sykes and the Black people of Maycomb.

statement: Mayella Ewell says that Tom Robinson attacked her.
Bob Ewell spits in Atticus's face after the trial.
After the trial, Tom Robinson goes home to his family.
explanation: Tom is sent to a prison farm, where he is shot while trying to escape.

statement: Scout's costume for the Halloween pageant is a cat.
explanation: She is dressed as a ham.

statement: Burris Ewell comes to school every day for the whole year.
explanation: He comes only on the first day, as the Ewell children always do.

statement: Bob Ewell has a steady job and looks after his family well.
explanation: The family lives on relief money, which Bob Ewell spends on whiskey.

statement: Miss Maudie is miserable after her house burns down.
explanation: She is cheerful. She says she always wanted a smaller house and a bigger garden.

statement: From the start, Atticus expects to win Tom Robinson's case.
explanation: He knows from the start that he will almost certainly lose.

statement: Mrs Dubose is addicted to morphine and wants to stop before she dies.
Atticus agrees to let Calpurnia go when Aunt Alexandra asks him to.
explanation: He refuses. He says Calpurnia is a faithful member of the family.

statement: Scout's conversation with Mr Cunningham helps to send the mob away from the jail.
Mr Underwood was protecting Atticus at the jail with a shotgun.
Mr Gilmer is Tom Robinson's lawyer.
explanation: Mr Gilmer is the prosecutor. Atticus defends Tom.

statement: Heck Tate says that Mayella's injuries were mostly on the right side of her face.
No doctor was called to examine Mayella.
Bob Ewell writes his name with his left hand.
Mayella says she has many friends in Maycomb.
explanation: She doesn't seem to know what Atticus means by friends. She is very lonely.

statement: Tom Robinson's left arm was badly injured in a cotton gin when he was a boy.
Tom says he felt sorry for Mayella, and this angers some people in the courtroom.
Dill cries in court because he is bored.
explanation: He is upset by the rude way Mr Gilmer speaks to Tom.

statement: Mr Dolphus Raymond only pretends to be drunk.
The jury reaches its verdict in a few minutes.
explanation: The jury is out for hours. It is late at night when they come back.

statement: Reverend Sykes tells Scout to stand up as her father leaves the courtroom.
The Black community ignores Atticus after the trial.
explanation: They leave a large amount of food at the Finches' house to thank him.

statement: Boo Radley's real name is Nathan.
explanation: Boo's real name is Arthur. Nathan is his older brother.

statement: Among the gifts in the tree are two soap figures that look like Jem and Scout.
Uncle Jack listens to Scout's side of the story before he punishes her for fighting Francis.
explanation: He punishes her first, and later admits he should have listened.

statement: Atticus believes that defending Tom will make his family more popular in Maycomb.
explanation: He expects the case to bring his family insults and trouble.

statement: Miss Maudie explains why Atticus says it is a sin to kill a mockingbird.
Jem only has to read to Mrs Dubose for one afternoon.
explanation: He reads to her every afternoon for more than a month.

statement: After her death, Mrs Dubose sends Jem a white camellia.
Atticus tells Jem that Mrs Dubose was the bravest person he ever knew.
Aunt Alexandra happily allows Scout to visit Calpurnia's house.
explanation: She refuses to let Scout go.

statement: The Ewells live in a large, well-kept house in the centre of Maycomb.
explanation: They live in a cabin behind the town rubbish dump.

statement: Jem expects the jury to find Tom guilty.
explanation: Jem is sure that Atticus has won.

statement: Atticus learns that one of the Cunninghams on the jury wanted to acquit Tom.
Atticus refuses to appeal against Tom's conviction.
explanation: He plans an appeal and tells Tom they have a good chance.

statement: Tom Robinson is shot seventeen times while trying to escape from prison.
In his newspaper, Mr Underwood compares Tom's death to the senseless killing of songbirds.
Miss Gates criticises Hitler's treatment of the Jews, but Scout has heard her speak badly about Black people.
Bob Ewell gets a job with the WPA but loses it within days.
Link Deas refuses to give Helen Robinson work after the trial.
explanation: He gives her a job and protects her from Bob Ewell.

statement: Atticus agrees at once with Heck Tate's account of how Bob Ewell died.
explanation: At first he thinks Jem killed Bob, and he does not want the truth hidden.

statement: Heck Tate decides to say that Bob Ewell fell on his own knife.
The novel is narrated by Scout as an adult, looking back on her childhood.
The Finches are newcomers to Maycomb County, with no family history there.
explanation: The family has lived at Finch's Landing since Simon Finch settled there generations ago.

statement: Atticus's legal career began with a defeat: his first two clients were hanged.
Atticus's brother Jack followed him into the law.
explanation: Jack studied medicine in Boston and is a doctor.

statement: Miss Caroline is a Maycomb native who understands the town's families.
explanation: She is from north Alabama and knows nothing of Maycomb's ways.

statement: The novel's title comes from a speech Atticus makes during the trial.
explanation: It comes from his warning to the children, when they get air rifles, that killing a mockingbird is a sin.

statement: Mrs Dubose dies still addicted to morphine.
explanation: She breaks her addiction before she dies, which is why Atticus calls her brave.

statement: Calpurnia speaks differently at church partly because people resent someone who seems to know more than they do.
At the jail, Scout mentions Mr Cunningham's entailment, a legal problem Atticus has been helping him with.
Mr Underwood protects Atticus because he sympathises with the Black community.
explanation: Atticus says Mr Underwood despises Black people. He protects Atticus all the same.

statement: Tom Robinson is the only witness Atticus calls for the defence.
Mr Dolphus Raymond pretends to be drunk to give people a reason for the way he lives.
In his closing speech, Atticus suggests that Mayella was beaten by someone who led with his left hand.
The novel is in two parts, and Tom Robinson's trial falls in the second.
Miss Maudie sees the length of the jury's discussion as a small step forward.
Jem comes to believe that Boo Radley stays inside because he wants to.
Atticus tells Tom he has no chance at all on appeal.
explanation: He tells Tom they have a good chance, though he cannot promise more.

statement: Bob Ewell attacks the children on their way to the Halloween pageant.
explanation: He attacks them on the way home, in the dark.

statement: Scout realises who rescued her as soon as she gets home on Halloween night.
explanation: She only recognises Boo Radley later, standing behind the door in Jem's room.

statement: The novel ends on the night of the verdict.
explanation: It ends months later, after Halloween, with Scout seeing her street from the Radley porch.
